title: Power Apps: model-driven apps as Business Applications in Work IQ
summary: Hold: the App Access instructions stop at enabling the control and omit choosing the applications to block. The Copilot Studio path also omits a documented section, and the checklist overstates the effect of unsupported custom controls and subgrids on record creation and updates.

claims.claim: Power Apps model-driven apps are available as Business Applications in Work IQ.
claims.quote: Power Apps model-driven apps are now available as Business Apps in Work IQ.

claims.quote: **European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments**: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **Government-related environments**: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: **Nonproduction environments**: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, third bullet
claims.claim: Create and update will not work through Work IQ in apps that use custom controls or subgrids.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ features are managed at Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote:
Select **Manage**, and select the environment.
Select **Settings** > **Product** > **Features**.
Locate **Work IQ**.

claims.claim: No API or CLI for the environment Work IQ feature toggle is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" environment setting Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell enable; "Work IQ" "PowerShell" "setting"; "Work IQ" "Power Platform API". Opened manage-participation and default-settings; no automation for this toggle found.

claims.claim: Environment administrators manage the environment Work IQ setting.
claims.quote: Environment administrators manage this setting.

claims.claim: The Copilot audience control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select **Copilot** > **Settings**.
In **Copilot settings**, select **View all** > **Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot**.

claims.claim: No API or CLI for the Business Applications Copilot audience setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Applications data" "Copilot" Microsoft Graph settings API. Opened default-settings and manage-ai-experience-access; reviewed Graph permissions search results. No operation for this audience setting found.

claims.claim: The audience choices are No users, Specific groups and All users, with All users the stated default.
claims.quote:
To turn off access for everyone, select **No users**.
To turn on access for everyone, select **All users**. This option is the default.
To provide access to a limited audience, select **Specific groups**, and then add or remove groups.

claims.claim: The tenant audience instructions require a tenant administrator account.
claims.quote: You need a tenant administrator account.

claims.claim: Learn does not state whether the Copilot audience control also governs the Copilot Studio tool.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Applications" "Work IQ" "Copilot Studio" "tenant" audience setting. Opened default-settings, manage-ai-experience-access and add-work-iq; the audience control is described for Microsoft 365 Copilot, not the Studio tool.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote:
Select **Agents** > **Tools**.
Select **Work IQ MCP**.
Review its current availability.
To block access to the server, select **Block**.
claims.fix: Append to controls[2].note: "The Copilot Studio Work IQ page says the ability to allow or disallow tooling and MCP servers might not yet be available in your region." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq.

claims.claim: No API or CLI for blocking the entire Work IQ MCP server is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" block server Microsoft Graph API admin; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "Work IQ" "block". Opened manage-ai-experience-access and policy-governance-mcp; no server availability automation found.

claims.claim: Security > Identity & access > App Access Control > environment > Enable > Save is the complete procedure for choosing which applications can access the environment.
claims.quote:
Select **Enable**, and then select **Save**.
Return to the environment and select the applications you want to block from accessing the environment.
claims.fix: Keep the documented path but append to controls[3].note and the corresponding rendered row: "After Enable > Save, return to the environment and select the applications you want to block from accessing it." The enablement steps alone do not choose the blocked applications.

claims.claim: No API or CLI for this App Access configuration is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "App Access Control" Power Platform API PowerShell CLI Dataverse; "app access control" "API" "configure". Opened manage-ai-experience-access; read control-app-access-environment excerpts and CLI reference results; no equivalent call found.

claims.claim: App participation is configured in Power Apps > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select **Apps**.
Find the app that you want to manage, and then select **Edit**.
On the app navigation bar, select **Settings**.
Select **Features**.
Set **Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps** to **On** or **Off**.
claims.fix: Append to controls[4].note: "The maker configuration page labels this option Microsoft Copilot in model-driven apps." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/add-microsoft-365-copilot#enable-microsoft-copilot-in-a-single-model-driven-app; retain the path supported by default-settings.

claims.claim: No API or CLI for the app-level m365copilotmodelappenabled setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "m365copilotmodelappenabled" API appsetting Web API; "m365copilotmodelappenabled" "setting" "API". Opened default-settings and use-business-apps-work-iq; read maker configuration excerpts. No setting-specific automation found.

claims.claim: Makers must save and publish the app after changing its Copilot setting.
claims.quote:
Set **Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps** to **On** or **Off**.
Select **Save**.
Select **Publish**.

claims.claim: The preview workload path is agent > ellipsis (...) > Settings > Work IQ > Enable preview workloads.
claims.quote:
In the **Agent settings** dialog, select **Work IQ**.
Under **Preview workloads**, turn on **Enable preview workloads**.
claims.fix: Replace controls[5].ui.path and the rendered path with "agent > ellipsis (...) > Settings > Work IQ > Preview workloads > Enable preview workloads" to include the documented section between Work IQ and the toggle.

claims.claim: No API or CLI for the agent's Enable preview workloads setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "Enable preview workloads" API Dataverse. Opened agents-experience/add-work-iq and reviewed search results; no Dataverse property, API operation or CLI equivalent for this toggle found.

claims.claim: Makers can remove Business apps from an agent by clearing that workload under Sources in the Work IQ tool.
claims.quote: In the **Edit tool** dialog, under **Sources**, clear the selection next to each workload you want to remove. Keep the workloads your agent needs selected.

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant-level setting prevents Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse data sharing even if an app is configured to share.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.claim: The default-settings page gives the full Business Applications data in Work IQ label, while the AI access page describes business applications availability.
claims.quote: Open the setting for **business applications availability** in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy documentation disallows mutation operations by default for its documented Microsoft 365 resource paths.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Whether the documented Work IQ MCP mutation policy governs Business Applications create, update and delete is not established by the cited pages.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Applications" "Work IQ" "tenant policy" mutation. Opened policy-governance-mcp and use-business-apps-work-iq; read tool-reference excerpts. Policy scope names Microsoft 365 resources; no Business Applications-specific applicability passage found.

claims.claim: Enabling environment Work IQ features is separate from allowing Work IQ to reason over the environment's data.
claims.quote: Enabling these features in an environment is a separate decision from allowing Work IQ to reason over that environment's data.
